title: Earle Dickson and the invention of the adhesive bandage (Band-Aid)

sources.title: A Revolution in Healing
sources.note: 只取「1920 年首度試賣」一項

facts.text: Earle Dickson worked for the company Johnson & Johnson as a cotton buyer.
Dickson's wife was Josephine Knight Dickson; the two married in 1917.
Josephine often got small cuts and burns on her fingers while working in the kitchen.
The bandages people used at that time were big and clumsy, and it was hard to put one on a wound by yourself; cloth wrappings did not stay in place well.
Johnson & Johnson already made surgical tape and gauze, but as two separate products.
Dickson's idea was to combine the two: he stuck small pieces of sterile gauze onto the middle of strips of surgical tape.
He covered the sticky side with crinoline, a stiff cloth, so the tape would not stick to itself, and rolled it up so a piece could be cut off whenever it was needed.
Josephine is given credit for helping him work out the idea.
The company's leaders became interested when Dickson showed that a person could put the bandage on without anyone else's help.
Johnson & Johnson first test-marketed the Band-Aid in 1920.
The first Band-Aids were made by hand and sold poorly; only about $3,000 worth were sold in the first year.
The early strips were 2½ inches wide and 18 inches long, and this size may be one reason they sold poorly.
Sales grew after Johnson & Johnson handed out large numbers of free Band-Aids to Boy Scout troops across the United States in the 1920s.
In 1924, Johnson & Johnson began making Band-Aids by machine, in several different sizes.
Band-Aids became fully sterilized in 1939.
A version made of thin vinyl was introduced in 1958.
Dickson received a U.S. patent for the bandage in 1926; that design looks much like the Band-Aid of today.
Dickson later became a vice president of Johnson & Johnson; he retired in 1957 and died in 1961.
In 2017, long after his death, Dickson was added to the National Inventors Hall of Fame.
More than 100 billion Band-Aids have been made.
The basic product has changed very little since it was first made.

notes: Band-Aid 是 Johnson & Johnson 的商標；文中只當作產品名稱提到。
